messages.content: Write a contemporary American fiction scene about two adult friends walking home together after school. The story is still in the walking-home portion of the scene. They have not reached the house yet. Keep them on the walk for the entire passage. Do not have them arrive, enter a building, get into a vehicle, or skip ahead in time. Output only story prose.

The sidewalk narrowed where the old tree roots had pushed the concrete up in uneven ridges.

“Careful,” Alex said.

“I see it.”

“You almost stepped on it.”

“I was testing you.”

Jordan stepped over the crack and kept going. “So, what are you doing Saturday?”

“Nothing yet.”

“That sounds suspicious.”

“It means nothing is planned.”

“Want to get breakfast?”

“Depends where.”

“Same place.”

“The place with the terrible coffee?”

“The coffee is fine.”

“It tastes like somebody described coffee to hot water.”

Jordan laughed. “You still drank two cups.”

“I was trying to make it work.”

They reached the crosswalk and waited for the signal.

“Your birthday's next month,” Jordan said.

“Don't remind me.”

“You getting old?”

“I’m getting expensive.”

“That doesn't even make sense.”

“Neither do birthday cards.”

The signal changed, and they crossed together. Jordan adjusted her backpack and glanced down the next block.

“Breakfast Saturday?”

“Yeah.”

“Good.”

They kept walking.
